New York hush money trial: defense rests (May 2024)

On Tuesday, 21 May 2024, Trump's lawyers rested their defense in his New York 'hush money' trial without calling him to the witness stand, moving the case toward jury deliberation.[{n}] Defense attorney [[todd-blanche|Todd Blanche]] told Judge [[juan-merchan|Juan M. Merchan]], 'Your honor, the defense rests,' after testimony from a former federal prosecutor who challenged the credibility of the prosecution's key witness.[{n}] As the first U.S. president to undergo a criminal trial, Trump declined to answer reporters' questions as he left the courthouse, including questions about his decision not to testify; the Republican presumptive presidential nominee had previously said he intended to take the stand.[{n}] Jurors were dismissed until 28 May for closing arguments, and after more than four weeks of testimony could begin deliberating on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records as soon as the following week.[{n}]
Defense rests in the New York hush money trial (2024)

On 21 May 2024, Blanche told Judge [[juan-merchan|Juan M. Merchan]], 'Your honor, the defense rests,' concluding the defense case in [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s New York hush money trial without Trump testifying.[{n}] The defense closed after testimony from a former federal prosecutor who attacked the credibility of the prosecution's principal witness.[{n}] Blanche also framed the core legal objection to the prosecution's theory, asking, 'How can withholding a false story from the voters be considered criminal?'— a formulation Badlands contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] cited in arguing that no underlying crime existed in the case.[{n}]
May 2024: close of the defense case

After the defense rested on 21 May 2024, Merchan advised jurors that the court session might extend late into the day to accommodate both prosecution and defense summations, which would represent the jury's final opportunity to hear from either side.[{n}] He dismissed the jury until 28 May, when closing arguments were scheduled, and attorneys were set to return later that Tuesday to discuss his instructions for deliberations.[{n}] Badlands contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] characterized the proceeding as a partisan political attack conducted in Merchan's courtroom and called for an inquiry into the judge's potential abuses of discretion.[{n}]
